---
title: "Preprocessor Directives in C#"
---

Lines that start with `#` in C# are called **preprocessor directives**. They are special instructions to the compiler that are processed *before* the actual compilation of your code.

Let me explain the most common ones:


## `#region` and `#endregion`

These are used for **code folding/organization**. They let you collapse and expand sections of code in your IDE.

```csharp
#region Private Helper Methods

private void ValidateInput(string input)
{
    // validation logic
}

private void LogError(string message)
{
    // logging logic
}

#endregion
```

**What it looks like in VS Code:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ▼ Private Helper Methods               │  ← Expanded (clickable)
│    private void ValidateInput(...) {}   │
│    private void LogError(...) {}        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ▶ Private Helper Methods ...           │  ← Collapsed (clickable)
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

> **Note:** `#region` has no effect on compilation—it's purely for code organization.


## Other Common Preprocessor Directives

| Directive | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `#if`, `#else`, `#elif`, `#endif` | Conditional compilation |
| `#define`, `#undef` | Define/undefine symbols |
| `#warning` | Emit a compiler warning |
| `#error` | Emit a compiler error |
| `#nullable` | Control nullable context |
| `#pragma` | Special compiler instructions |


## Example: Conditional Compilation

```csharp
#define DEBUG_MODE

public void ProcessData()
{
    #if DEBUG_MODE
        Console.WriteLine("Debug: Processing started...");
    #endif
    
    // actual processing code
    
    #if DEBUG_MODE
        Console.WriteLine("Debug: Processing completed.");
    #else
        // production-only code
    #endif
}
```

This is useful when you want different behavior in **Debug** vs **Release** builds.


## Key Difference from Comments

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Comments           vs      Preprocessor Directives      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  // single line              #region                     │
│  /* multi-line */            #if DEBUG                   │
│                                                          │
│  → Ignored by compiler       → Processed BEFORE compile  │
│  → Just for humans           → Can change what compiles  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Practical Tip

In modern C#, `#region` is somewhat debated:

- **Pro:** Helps organize large files
- **Con:** Can hide code complexity; some prefer smaller classes instead
